summary: New after v1.0.203: choose Android noise suppression or the APK-bundled GTCRN denoiser for private offline blue-mic dictation; compare one actual microphone take in BR Brain, with native-crash isolation and raw-speech fallback.

changes.title: Two selectable voice-noise engines, one mic capture
changes.detail: BR Brain → Voice & Noise Reduction now selects either Android's capture-time NoiseSuppressor or brrBoard's already-bundled GTCRN model running after capture. The choice also applies to the normal blue offline mic. Only one AudioRecord is opened. GTCRN inference runs in a separate, non-exported short-lived Android process, with a 17-second parent timeout and automatic original-audio fallback if it crashes or cannot enhance. Existing Parakeet 110M, package, original signing certificate and offline/no-Internet design remain unchanged.

changes.title: Replay identical raw and processed audio
changes.detail: The lab now performs one explicit 12-second RAM-only recording per test. In GTCRN mode, its Original and GTCRN playback use exactly the same captured microphone sample; users can independently score both versions against the chosen English/Hinglish sentence. Android NoiseSuppressor cannot be post-applied to stored PCM, so OS-vs-GTCRN remains two distinct capture-time modes, not a fabricated same-take comparison.

changes.title: Guard failed earbuds and native noise processing
changes.detail: The lab explicitly rejects a missing or refused Bluetooth microphone, rejects near-silent input, detects a mismatched Android-reported route and checks capture-silenced state where supported. GTCRN does not run on every keystroke, on an active call or for long dictation exceeding the bounded Binder transfer. Model failures do not propagate into the live keyboard process; its original speech can still be recognized.
